chapter: In The Mood, Rendezvous and Capitol
title: Recording In The Mood and Christopher Columbus; the trade reviews
summary: Fields reads the July 1959 Cash Box review of Rendezvous 110, with Love noting composer Joe Garland and explaining the backing vocals.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: So I went on out there and that's when we did all of this Rendevous stuff. We did "In The Mood", we did "Christopher Columbus".
Kind of a rhythm and blues, rock version of it.
We did all of those things and then it just went right on. The first thing that happened, after I went on, when I was in Oklahoma, and I have here the date it was released--
This is record reviewers-- what is the date here?
We first started in fifty-eight, you remember, and Rene said go on in and come
Let me read this. They gave you a B plus; Cash Box.
"In The Mood, Shapiro, Bernstein, Rasoff, Garland--Joe Garland--

He was with Armstrong's band, he was his bandleader. In fact, I was with Lucky Millinder and he was with Cecil Scott's band and we used to talk and that tune keeps him well off. I was just at a college doing a residency last week and all of them has In The Mood, so Joe Garland has money coming in.
"The Glenn Miller favorite, excitingly in tune with teen tastes, this instrumental sparker to come on big. Watch it." Ernie Fields, Rendezvous 110. And the Christopher
Columbus, it says another revival of an oldie for teen tastes, and results in making the grade too. (Inaudible) songsters are included here, two tracks--you had some girls?
